title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — Judah Gen 43 & Bathsheba: 'I will sin' = be held guilty
pass_a_gloss: Judah to Jacob (Gen 43): if I fail to return Benjamin, I shall have sinned—that is, I shall be held guilty. Bathsheba to David (1 Kgs 1:21): we shall be sinners means we shall be treated as the guilty. That is the force of the opponent's move at this step.
pass_b_english: As when Judah, about to take Benjamin with him into Egypt, addresses his father Jacob thus, Genesis XLIII. I pledge for him; of my hand require him: If I do not bring him back to you, and set him before you, I shall altogether have sinned against you all my days, that is, I shall be guilty to you, and shall be held by you for a criminal: So Bathsheba to David, 1 Kings I. 21. when the lord king sleeps with his fathers, I and my son Solomon shall be sinners; that is, it shall be dealt with us as with the guilty and the accused, as the interpreters explain.
source_text: Ut cum Iudas secum Beniaminem in Aegyptum abducturus, patrem Iacobum ita alloquitur, Genes. XLIII. Ego spondeo pro eo, de manu mea reposcito eum: Si non reduxero eum ad te, & statuero eum coram te, omnino peccavero tibi omnibus diebus, id est, ero tibi reus, & a te habebor pro scelerato: Sic Bethsabea ad Davidem 1. Regum I. 21. cum occubuerit Dominus Iesus Rex cum patribus suis, ego & filius meus Schelomoh erimus peccatores; id est, agetur nobiscum tanquam cum sontibus & reis, ut exponunt interpretes.
